subject: The one mistake I made building this app
preview_text: I wasn't going to send this email. But I realized something about the feature 90% of users skip.
body_paragraphs: I was looking at our data last night. The numbers are good. 110+ dogs healthier. But one stat kept me up. It's about the before/after photo timeline. Almost nobody uses it. And that's my fault.

I don't usually write emails like this, but I need to confess something. I built that feature for the 'after' photo. The victory shot. The leaner, happier dog. But I was wrong. The real magic is in the 'before'. The photo you take today, when you're not proud, when you see your best friend struggling. That photo is your 'why'. It's the anchor. It's what you look at on day 3 when you're tempted to skip the walk.

That timeline isn't a trophy case. It's a visual diary of your commitment. It turns guilt into a graph of love. Every time you log a weight, you can tap that camera icon and see the story you're writing. Not for Instagram. For your dog's heartbeat.

Open the app right now. Go to the Progress tab. Tap 'Add Photo'. Take one picture. Just one. For future you. For the day your dog runs to the park like a puppy again. P.S. The users who use the timeline feature are 3x more likely to hit their dog's goal weight. They have the proof.
